prompt: Stage 3-2 augment round, level 6 with 62 gold at 46 HP on a 6-loss streak you started on purpose at 2-2. You hold a 1-star 3-cost AD carry with two completed AD items, a second copy on the bench, and a 2-star 3-cost tank. Stage-3 losses cost 6 to 8 HP; stage 4 will cost 12 to 16. When does the loss streak end?

options.label: Now. Level to 7, roll to ~30 for 2-star 3-costs, and start winning at 3-2: you are below 50 HP with three stage-3 fights left and stage 4 damage ahead
At 4-1: two more rounds of streak gold and interest, then level 8 with 80 gold
At 3-5: one more round of income, then roll at level 6

explanation:
A loss streak is a loan against HP, and the exit condition is set by the repayment: you stop when the next losses start costing more than the streak pays, or when the HP left cannot absorb the stage-4 damage you will take before the board is good. At 46 HP, three more stage-3 losses leave you at roughly 25 entering stage 4, where a single miss on the 4-1 rolldown ends the game. The streak has done its job: 62 gold at 3-2 with the augment in hand is exactly what it was for.

Waiting to 4-1 for 'level 8 with 80 gold' is the plan that sounds like Master and plays like 8th: the extra 18 gold buys nine rolls and costs 25 HP, and the board at 4-1 must hit on the first rolldown or die. Stopping at 3-2 gives you three rounds at level 7 to convert gold into 2-stars with fights that only cost 8 when you lose. The 3-5 option is the half-measure: one more round of losses for one more round of income, at a level where rolling barely finds 3-costs.
principle: A loss streak ends when the HP left cannot pay for the losses between now and a stable board. Set that number before you start streaking.
commonMistake: Extending a loss streak past 50 HP because the gold looks good and the board 'will come together at 8'.
